clue.text: Beat music rocking hot stuff perhaps

parts.note: to cap something is to beat or outdo it, as in capping a rival's story

indicators.note: rocking is moving to and fro, so the letters of the word before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pounding rock music is maybe something exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' reads as a noun beside music but is a verb, to cap. 'rocking' rearranges MUSIC into SICUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsicum is a pepper, and some peppers such as chillies are fiery, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Sailor back in the money in area of Marrakech?

indicators.note: in tells us the turned sailor sits inside the word for the money

parts.note: cash is money in notes and coins

indicators.note: back means the word for sailor is read from right to left

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a standard abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman is flush again while visiting part of a Moroccan city.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two 'in's: only the first is the container signal, working with 'back'; the second merely links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A casbah is the old citadel quarter of a North African city, and Marrakech has one; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Bowl over and wheeze endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for wheeze loses its final letter

parts.note: a wheeze is British slang for a clever scheme or trick, which is also a stunt
the final letter of the word for wheeze, which the indicator removes

explanation.surface: Someone is knocked flat and left gasping for breath without a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheeze' is not laboured breathing: in British slang it is a clever trick, a STUNT, which 'endlessly' cuts short by its last T.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs meaning to amaze or overwhelm someone.

clue.text: Complaint from conservative country stopping hostilities

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, as a cork stops a bottle, so these two pieces go inside the word for hostilities

parts.note: action is military fighting, as in 'killed in action'
the USA is a country

explanation.surface: A right-leaning nation halting a war draws a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal charge laid against someone is a grievance in the legal sense.

clue.text: Fortunate very recently too

parts.note: just means only a moment ago, as in 'she has just left'
a three-word way of saying also or in addition

explanation.surface: Someone has had good luck lately, on top of everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said of a lucky outcome: 'it's lucky you came' says the same thing.

clue.text: Plant in shelter close to park

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so this takes the final letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: Something growing in a covered spot near the green.
explanation.definitionFit: A leek is a vegetable of the onion family, one kind of growing thing.

clue.text: Novel is already having length cut possibly

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters that follow are put in a new order
cut says the abbreviation for length is removed from the words before it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A book is by now perhaps being shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' is not a book but the anagram signal; 'cut' takes L out of 'is already', leaving ISAREADY to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: As a sentence adverb the phrase means 'probably' or 'I suppose', expressing likelihood.

clue.text: A boring sign of a house shrew

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the clue's first word goes inside the star sign

parts.note: Virgo is a sign of the zodiac, whose twelve divisions astrologers call houses

explanation.surface: A tedious indication that a scold lives in the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated terms for a bad-tempered, scolding woman.

clue.text: Swivelling to serve food's somewhat different

indicators.note: swivelling means turning round, so the word for to serve is read backwards

parts.note: to do is to serve or suffice, as in 'that will do'
a dish is a prepared item of food

explanation.surface: Turning round to hand out a meal is a slightly unusual thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swivelling' turns DO (to serve, as in 'that will do') into OD; the 's on food is only the surface's 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd means unusual, and the suffix -ish softens it to 'rather unusual'.

clue.text: Names, initially missed, accommodating judge repeats

indicators.note: accommodating means housing, so the shortened word has the word for judge inside it
initially missed says the word for names loses its first letter

parts.note: to cite someone is to name them, as in citing a source
the first letter of the word for names, which the indicator removes
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A roll of names, skipped at first, makes room for a magistrate who says things again.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, a synonym in the same verb form.

clue.text: Worry if chapter is read out

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like a word for chapter

parts.note: a chapter of one's life is a phase or period

explanation.surface: Be anxious when a section of the book is recited.
explanation.definitionFit: To faze someone is to disconcert or trouble them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Not a queer time, oddly, for one ready to comment

indicators.note: oddly means strangely, so the letters before it are put into a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: It is, strangely, an unremarkable moment for a pundit eager to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tempts you to take odd letters, but here it is the anagram signal, covering 'Not a queer' plus T for time.
explanation.definitionFit: British journalists' slang for a pundit or politician who will supply an opinion on anything at a moment's notice.

clue.text: Painter, British, with excessive coolness, poor on reflection

parts.note: OTT, short for over the top, means excessive
ice stands for coldness of manner, as in an icy reception

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word for poor is read backwards

parts.note: ill means poor or bad, as in ill health or ill fortune

explanation.surface: A British artist, far too aloof, turns out to be bad when you think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns ILL into LLI. OTT is British shorthand for 'over the top'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandro Botticelli was the Florentine Renaissance artist who painted The Birth of Venus.

clue.text: United in key shoot-out?

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for United inside the word for key

parts.note: Del is the delete key on a computer keyboard
U is the abbreviation for United, as in the football club Man U

explanation.surface: Manchester United taking part in a crucial penalty decider.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight with pistols is a contest of firing at each other; the question mark admits swords are possible too.

clue.text: Lord's decision? Everyone's backing aristocrat

indicators.note: backing means standing behind, so the word for everyone follows the word for aristocrat

parts.note: a nob is British slang for a person of high social rank
the whole lot of people, in a three-letter word

explanation.surface: A peer makes a ruling and the whole chamber supports the nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is a London cricket ground, not a peer: the decision is an umpire's call of an illegal delivery. 'backing' puts ALL behind NOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord's is a London cricket ground, where an umpire's call of an illegal delivery is one such ruling.

clue.text: Sugar from pear — a remedy from the east

indicators.note: from the east says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sweetener made out of fruit, which is a cure brought from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'from the east' means right to left: the run ARAREMED, spanning 'pear — a remedy', is read from its far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a pale brown cane variety, named after a region of Guyana.

clue.text: Speechless when answer seemed to be about right at the end

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer, as in Q and A

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for seemed to be goes round the letter picked next

parts.note: sounded means seemed, as in 'it sounded true'

indicators.note: at the end picks the final letter of the word right

explanation.surface: Someone is struck dumb as a reply turned out to be roughly correct in the final reckoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amazed is often lost for words, so the two are loose synonyms.

clue.text: Politician new in constituency, extremely overfamiliar

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for new inside the word for constituency

parts.note: a seat is a parliamentary constituency, as in 'a safe seat'
N is the abbreviation for new, as in NT for New Testament

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, taken here from overfamiliar

explanation.surface: A newly arrived member is far too chummy with the locals.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, so one kind of elected legislator.

clue.text: Anarchy after Democrat leaves republic very upset

indicators.note: leaves says the abbreviation for Democrat departs from the word for republic

parts.note: Chad is a republic in central Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means overturned, so the word for very is read upwards

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so kind'

explanation.surface: Disorder follows when a Democrat quits the country in great distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Both name a state of total disorder with nobody in control.

clue.text: Name for any Yank's coat

definitions.meaning: an informal American way of addressing a man whose name you do not know, like 'buddy'
short for mackintosh, the British word for a raincoat

explanation.surface: What to call the jacket any American wears.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal American address for an unknown man is also the short form of mackintosh, a raincoat.

clue.text: Nice way to announce one's resignation?

definitions.text: Nice way to announce one's resignation?

parts.words: Nice way to announce one's resignation?
parts.note: Nice is the French city, so the way is a French one, and resignation is acceptance of one's lot, not quitting a job

explanation.surface: A pleasant manner of telling the boss you are quitting.
explanation.definitionFit: The French shrug meaning 'that's life' voices resigned acceptance, and Nice is a city in France.

clue.text: Learner welcomed by me, a newcomer, perhaps

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in, so the learner's letter goes inside the word for me

parts.note: the clue's writer is the crossword setter, so me is the setter
L is the plate a learner driver shows in Britain

explanation.surface: A novice is greeted by the speaker, who may be new here too.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler arrives to live in a new place, an example of a recent arrival.

clue.text: Scoffed about working for pay

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for scoffed surrounds the word for working

parts.note: to scoff is British slang for to eat greedily, so scoffed is ate
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: Someone sneered at the idea of labouring for wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' is not mockery here: in British slang to scoff food is to eat it greedily. The signal 'about' is a container, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends for a wrong is to suffer its cost, as in 'he will pay for his sins'.

clue.text: See boy describing places ultimately like paradise

indicators.note: describing means tracing a path round, as a compass describes a circle, so the two joined words go round the picked letter

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire and so a bishop's see
Ian is a boy's name

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the word places

explanation.surface: Watch a lad telling of spots that are, in the end, heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a noun, not a verb: a bishop's diocese, here a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire. 'describing' makes the see and the boy together go round the letter 'ultimately' picks.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysium was the Greek abode of the blessed dead, so the adjective means heavenly or blissful.

clue.text: Riles chap, awkwardly turning round

indicators.note: turning awkwardly suggests clumsy movement, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: It annoys a fellow who is clumsily spinning about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning round' looks like one reversal instruction, but 'round' alone is the definition and 'awkwardly turning' rearranges 'Riles chap'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a ball, so the adjective means ball-shaped.

clue.text: This is sure bet, eg to get drunk

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and muddled, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Here is a certain way, for instance, of becoming intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'This' is the definition, but the whole clue describes it: a pub's visiting ale is a sure way to get tipsy. 'to get drunk' rearranges 'sure bet, eg'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points at the answer, a pub's visiting ale, which the rest of the clue describes as reliably intoxicating.

clue.text: Sloth of ruling monarch papists regularly brought up

parts.note: the party in power is said to be in
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth II

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means the picked letters are read from the bottom upwards
regularly takes every second letter of the word papists

explanation.surface: The laziness of a reigning king is something Catholics were routinely raised with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes A, I, T from papists and 'brought up' turns them into TIA. ER is the cipher of the late Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is laziness, and the answer is a disinclination to move or act.

clue.text: A small pair of foreign articles in bits

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
un is the French for a or an, the first of the two articles
der is a German word for the, the second of the two articles

explanation.surface: A little couple of imported items lie broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Something torn apart is in pieces, which is the adverb's meaning.

clue.text: In the past travel to one's heart's content

parts.note: the word that follows a length of time to mean before now, as in 'long since'
to travel is to move from place to place, in a two-letter verb

explanation.surface: Formerly, people journeyed as much as they pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: From French, the phrase means in abundance or as much as you like, as in 'whisky a gogo'.

clue.text: A team honour principle

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, the size of a cricket or football side
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: One side respects a moral rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth taken as a starting point is a basic rule of reasoning.

clue.text: Son of flipping painter? Not one bit!

indicators.note: not says the piece named after it is taken away from the turned name
flipping means turning over, so the painter's name is read backwards

parts.note: Salvador Dali was the Spanish surrealist painter
one is I in Roman numerals, and bit marks it as a single piece of the name

explanation.surface: Is he the child of that blasted artist? Absolutely not!
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' is a mild British swear word in the surface but here turns DALI into ILAD; 'Not' then removes the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy is someone's male child, a loose synonym.
